16: # Cloud Network Security
17: 
18: Manage network security policies for Elastic Cloud Serverless projects: IP filters to allowlist specific IPs or CIDRs,
19: and VPC filters (AWS PrivateLink) to restrict traffic to specific VPC endpoints.
20: 
21: > **Prerequisite:** This skill assumes the **cloud-setup** skill has already run — `EC_API_KEY` is set in the
22: > environment and the organization context is established. If `EC_API_KEY` is missing, instruct the agent to invoke
23: > **cloud-setup** first. Do NOT prompt the user for an API key directly.
24: 
25: For project creation and day-2 operations (including associating filters with projects), see **cloud-create-project**
26: and **cloud-manage-project**. For identity and access management (users, roles, API keys), see
27: **cloud-access-management**.
28: 
29: For detailed API endpoints and request schemas, see [references/api-reference.md](references/api-reference.md).
30: 
31: ## Terminology
32: 
33: This skill uses **network security** as the umbrella term, aligned with the Elastic Cloud UI direction. The underlying
34: API uses **traffic filters** — you will see `traffic-filters` in endpoint paths and `traffic_filters` in JSON fields.
35: When a user or agent says "traffic filter," they mean the same thing as "network security policy." The two filter types
36: are **IP filters** (type `ip`) and **VPC filters** (type `vpce`).
37: 
38: ## Jobs to Be Done
39: 
40: - Create an IP filter to restrict ingress to specific IPs or CIDR blocks
41: - Create a VPC filter (AWS PrivateLink) to restrict traffic to specific VPC endpoint IDs
42: - List, inspect, update, and delete network security policies
43: - Look up PrivateLink region metadata (service names, domain names, availability zones)
44: - Associate or disassociate filters with Serverless projects (delegates to **cloud-manage-project**)
45: - Audit the current network security posture for an organization
46: 
47: ## Prerequisites and permissions
48: 
49: | Item            | Description                                                                                 |
50: | --------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
51: | **EC_API_KEY**  | Cloud API key (set by **cloud-setup**). Required for all operations.                        |
52: | **Region**      | Filters are region-scoped. The user must specify the target region when creating filters.   |
53: | **Project IDs** | Required only when associating filters with projects (handled by **cloud-manage-project**). |
54: 
55: Run `python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py list-filters` to verify that `EC_API_KEY`
56: is valid before proceeding with any operation.
57: 
58: ### Operation-level permissions
59: 
60: The following permissions are required for common network security operations in Elastic Cloud Serverless.
61: 
62: | Operation                        | Required permission                       |
63: | -------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- |
64: | List filters / get metadata      | Any organization member                   |
65: | Create / update / delete filters | Organization owner (`organization-admin`) |
66: | Associate filters with projects  | Organization owner or project Admin       |
67: 
68: This skill does not perform a separate role pre-check. Attempt the requested operation and let the API enforce
69: authorization. If the API returns an authorization error (for example, `403 Forbidden`), stop and ask the user to verify
70: the provided API key permissions.
71: 
72: ### Manual setup fallback (when cloud-setup is unavailable)
73: 
74: If this skill is installed standalone and `cloud-setup` is not available, instruct the user to configure Cloud
75: environment variables manually before running commands. Never ask the user to paste API keys in chat.
76: 
77: | Variable      | Required | Description                                                                          |
78: | ------------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
79: | `EC_API_KEY`  | Yes      | Elastic Cloud API key (see permissions table above for required roles by operation). |
80: | `EC_BASE_URL` | No       | Cloud API base URL (default: `https://api.elastic-cloud.com`).                       |
81: 
82: > **Note:** If `EC_API_KEY` is missing, or the user does not have a Cloud API key yet, direct the user to generate one
83: > at [Elastic Cloud API keys](https://cloud.elastic.co/account/keys), then configure it locally using the steps below.
84: 
85: Preferred method (agent-friendly): create a `.env` file in the project root:
86: 
87: ```bash
88: EC_API_KEY=your-api-key
89: EC_BASE_URL=https://api.elastic-cloud.com
90: ```
91: 
92: All `cloud/*` scripts auto-load `.env` from the working directory.
93: 
94: Alternative: export directly in the terminal:
95: 
96: ```bash
97: export EC_API_KEY="<your-cloud-api-key>"
98: export EC_BASE_URL="https://api.elastic-cloud.com"
99: ```
100: 
101: Terminal exports may not be visible to sandboxed agents running in separate shell sessions, so prefer `.env` when using
102: an agent.
103: 
104: ## Decomposing Network Security Requests
105: 
106: When the user describes a network security need in natural language (for example, "restrict my search project to our
107: office IP"), break the request into discrete tasks before executing.
108: 
109: ### Step 1 — Identify the components
110: 
111: | Component       | Question to answer                                                     |
112: | --------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------- |
113: | **Filter type** | IP filter (public IPs/CIDRs) or VPC filter (AWS PrivateLink endpoint)? |
114: | **Region**      | Which AWS region are the target projects in?                           |
115: | **Rules**       | What source IPs, CIDRs, or VPC endpoint IDs should be allowed?         |
116: | **Scope**       | Apply to all new projects by default, or specific projects only?       |
117: | **Projects**    | Which existing projects should this filter be associated with?         |
118: 
119: ### Step 2 — Check existing state
120: 
121: Before creating a new filter, check what already exists:
122: 
123: ```bash
124: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py list-filters --region us-east-1
125: ```
126: 
127: **Filter hygiene:** If an existing filter already covers the same source rules **for the same purpose**, reuse it
128: instead of creating a duplicate. Filters are region-scoped and can be associated with multiple projects, so a single
129: filter with the right rules serves many projects. Two filters with identical source rules are fine when they serve
130: different purposes (for example, different teams managing their own policies), but creating a second filter for the same
131: purpose is unnecessary.
132: 
133: ### Step 3 — Create the filter
134: 
135: Run the appropriate command from `skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py`.
136: 
137: ### Step 4 — Associate with projects
138: 
139: Filter association is managed using the project PATCH endpoint. Use **cloud-manage-project** to associate or
140: disassociate filters:
141: 
142: ```text
143: PATCH /api/v1/serverless/projects/{type}/{id}
144: Body: { "traffic_filters": [{ "id": "filter-id-1" }, { "id": "filter-id-2" }] }
145: ```
146: 
147: When updating associations, provide the **complete list** of filter IDs. Any filter not included in the list is
148: disassociated from the project.
149: 
150: ### Step 5 — Verify
151: 
152: After execution, list filters again or GET the project to confirm the change took effect.
153: 
154: ## IP Filters versus VPC Filters
155: 
156: | Aspect            | IP Filter (`ip`)                                   | VPC Filter (`vpce`)                                      |
157: | ----------------- | -------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------- |
158: | **Purpose**       | Allowlist public IP addresses or CIDR blocks       | Restrict traffic to specific AWS VPC endpoint IDs        |
159: | **Use case**      | Office IPs, CI/CD runners, partner access          | Private connectivity without public internet exposure    |
160: | **Source format** | IP address or CIDR (for example, `203.0.113.0/24`) | AWS VPC endpoint ID (for example, `vpce-0abc123def456`)  |
161: | **Network path**  | Public internet                                    | AWS PrivateLink (private, never leaves AWS network)      |
162: | **Prerequisite**  | None                                               | VPC endpoint and DNS record created in AWS console first |
163: 
164: > **Key concept:** Private connectivity in AWS is accepted by default in Elastic Cloud. Creating a VPC filter is only
165: > needed to **restrict** traffic to specific VPC endpoint IDs. If you only need private connectivity (without
166: > filtering), create the VPC endpoint and DNS record in AWS — no filter is needed on the Elastic Cloud side.
167: 
168: ## Examples
169: 
170: ### Allowlist an office IP range
171: 
172: **Prompt:** "Only allow traffic from our office network 203.0.113.0/24 to projects in us-east-1."
173: 
174: ```bash
175: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py create-filter \
176:   --name "Office IP allowlist" \
177:   --type ip \
178:   --region us-east-1 \
179:   --rules '[{"source": "203.0.113.0/24", "description": "Office network"}]'
180: ```
181: 
182: Then associate the filter with specific projects using **cloud-manage-project**.
183: 
184: ### Restrict traffic to a VPC endpoint
185: 
186: **Prompt:** "Lock down my observability project to only accept traffic from our VPC endpoint."
187: 
188: ```bash
189: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py create-filter \
190:   --name "Production VPC" \
191:   --type vpce \
192:   --region us-east-1 \
193:   --rules '[{"source": "vpce-0abc123def456", "description": "Production VPC endpoint"}]'
194: ```
195: 
196: ### List all filters in a region
197: 
198: **Prompt:** "Show me all network security policies in eu-west-1."
199: 
200: ```bash
201: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py list-filters --region eu-west-1
202: ```
203: 
204: ### Update a filter to add a new IP
205: 
206: **Prompt:** "Add the VPN IP 198.51.100.5 to our existing office filter."
207: 
208: ```bash
209: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py get-filter --filter-id tf-12345
210: # Review current rules, then update with the complete rule set:
211: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py update-filter \
212:   --filter-id tf-12345 \
213:   --body '{"rules": [{"source": "203.0.113.0/24", "description": "Office network"}, {"source": "198.51.100.5", "description": "VPN"}]}'
214: ```
215: 
216: ### Look up PrivateLink metadata for a region
217: 
218: **Prompt:** "What PrivateLink service name do I need for us-east-1?"
219: 
220: ```bash
221: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py get-metadata --region us-east-1
222: ```
223: 
224: ### Delete an unused filter
225: 
226: **Prompt:** "Remove the old staging IP filter."
227: 
228: ```bash
229: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py delete-filter --filter-id tf-67890 --dry-run
230: # Review what would be deleted, then confirm:
231: python3 skills/cloud/network-security/scripts/cloud_network_security.py delete-filter --filter-id tf-67890
232: ```
233: 
234: ## Guidelines
235: 
236: - If `EC_API_KEY` is not set, do not prompt the user — instruct the agent to invoke **cloud-setup** first.
237: - Always confirm destructive actions (delete filter) with the user before executing.
238: - Filters are **region-scoped**: a filter created in `us-east-1` can only be associated with projects in that region.
239: - **Filter hygiene — reuse, scope, and clean up:**
240:   - Before creating a filter, always run `list-filters` and check whether an existing filter **for the same purpose**
241:     already has the required source rules. Filters can be associated with multiple projects, so one filter with the
242:     right rules is better than duplicates.
243:   - Duplicate filters means filters for the same purpose with identical source rules — not merely overlapping IPs. Two
244:     filters covering different project groups with the same CIDR are legitimate.
245:   - Review unused filters periodically. If a filter is no longer associated with any project, prompt the user to delete
246:     it to reduce clutter.
247: - **Updating rules replaces the entire rule set.** When adding a rule using PATCH, include all existing rules plus the
248:   new one. Omitting an existing rule removes it.
249: - **Deleting a filter fails if it is still associated with a project.** Disassociate first using
250:   **cloud-manage-project** (PATCH the project with the filter removed from the `traffic_filters` list), then delete.
251: - `include_by_default` automatically associates the filter with all new projects in the region. Use with caution — it
252:   affects every future project.
253: - For project association and disassociation, delegate to the **cloud-manage-project** skill. This skill manages filter
254:   definitions only.
255: - For identity and access management (users, roles, API keys), see **cloud-access-management**.

28: ## Traffic Filters
29: 
30: > **Official API docs:**
31: > [Serverless traffic filter endpoints](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elastic-cloud-serverless/group/endpoint-traffic-filters)
32: 
33: ### List traffic filters
34: 
35: ```text
36: GET /api/v1/serverless/traffic-filters
37: ```
38: 
39: Returns all traffic filters for the authenticated organization.
40: 
41: **Query parameters:**
42: 
43: | Parameter            | Type    | Required | Description                             |
44: | -------------------- | ------- | -------- | --------------------------------------- |
45: | `region`             | string  | No       | Limit results to this region only       |
46: | `include_by_default` | boolean | No       | Filter by the `include_by_default` flag |
47: 
48: **Response (200):**
49: 
50: ```json
51: {
52:   "items": [
53:     {
54:       "id": "tf-12345",
55:       "name": "Office IP allowlist",
56:       "description": "Allow office network",
57:       "type": "ip",
58:       "include_by_default": false,
59:       "region": "us-east-1",
60:       "rules": [{ "source": "203.0.113.0/24", "description": "Office network" }]
61:     }
62:   ]
63: }
64: ```
65: 
66: ### Create a traffic filter
67: 
68: ```text
69: POST /api/v1/serverless/traffic-filters
70: ```
71: 
72: Creates a traffic filter consisting of a set of rules.
73: 
74: **Request body:** [TrafficFilterRequest](#trafficfilterrequest)
75: 
76: **Response (201):** [TrafficFilterInfo](#trafficfilterinfo) — includes the generated `id`.
77: 
78: **Example — IP filter:**
79: 
80: ```json
81: {
82:   "name": "Office IPs",
83:   "description": "Corporate office allowlist",
84:   "type": "ip",
85:   "region": "us-east-1",
86:   "include_by_default": false,
87:   "rules": [
88:     { "source": "203.0.113.0/24", "description": "Office network" },
89:     { "source": "198.51.100.5", "description": "VPN gateway" }
90:   ]
91: }
92: ```
93: 
94: **Example — VPC filter (AWS PrivateLink):**
95: 
96: ```json
97: {
98:   "name": "Production VPC",
99:   "description": "Restrict to production VPC endpoint",
100:   "type": "vpce",
101:   "region": "us-east-1",
102:   "include_by_default": false,
103:   "rules": [{ "source": "vpce-0abc123def456", "description": "Production VPC endpoint" }]
104: }
105: ```
106: 
107: ### Get a traffic filter
108: 
109: ```text
110: GET /api/v1/serverless/traffic-filters/{id}
111: ```
112: 
113: Retrieves a single traffic filter by ID.
114: 
115: **Path parameters:**
116: 
117: | Parameter | Type   | Required | Description           |
118: | --------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------- |
119: | `id`      | string | Yes      | The traffic filter ID |
120: 
121: **Response (200):** [TrafficFilterInfo](#trafficfilterinfo)
122: 
123: ### Update a traffic filter
124: 
125: ```text
126: PATCH /api/v1/serverless/traffic-filters/{id}
127: ```
128: 
129: Partially updates a traffic filter. Only include the fields to change.
130: 
131: **Path parameters:**
132: 
133: | Parameter | Type   | Required | Description           |
134: | --------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------- |
135: | `id`      | string | Yes      | The traffic filter ID |
136: 
137: **Request body:** [PatchTrafficFilterRequest](#patchtrafficfilterrequest)
138: 
139: **Response (200):** [TrafficFilterInfo](#trafficfilterinfo)
140: 
141: > **Important:** When updating `rules`, provide the **complete** rule set. Any rules not included in the update are
142: > removed. To add a rule, include all existing rules plus the new one.
143: 
144: ### Delete a traffic filter
145: 
146: ```text
147: DELETE /api/v1/serverless/traffic-filters/{id}
148: ```
149: 
150: Deletes a traffic filter by ID. Fails with `400` if the filter is still associated with a project. Disassociate the
151: filter from all projects first using the project PATCH endpoint.
152: 
153: **Path parameters:**
154: 
155: | Parameter | Type   | Required | Description           |
156: | --------- | ------ | -------- | --------------------- |
157: | `id`      | string | Yes      | The traffic filter ID |
158: 
159: **Response (200):** Empty response on success.
160: 
161: **Error (400):** Returns an error if the filter is associated with a project:
162: 
163: ```json
164: {
165:   "errors": [{ "message": "traffic filter is associated with <project-id>, remove the association first" }]
166: }
167: ```

186:

192:

196:     {
197:       "region": "us-east-1",

199:       "domain_name": "private.us-east-1.aws.elastic.cloud",
200:       "availability_zones": ["use1-az2", "use1-az4", "use1-az6"]

202:   ]
203: }

208: ## Schemas
209: 
210: ### TrafficFilterRequest
211: 
212: Used when creating a traffic filter (`POST`).
213: 
214: | Field                | Type    | Required | Description                                                         |
215: | -------------------- | ------- | -------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------- |
216: | `name`               | string  | Yes      | Display name for the filter                                         |
217: | `description`        | string  | No       | Human-readable description                                          |
218: | `type`               | string  | No       | `ip` (default) or `vpce`                                            |
219: | `region`             | string  | Yes      | AWS region the filter applies to                                    |
220: | `include_by_default` | boolean | No       | Auto-associate with all new projects in the region (default: false) |
221: | `rules`              | array   | No       | List of [TrafficFilterRule](#trafficfilterrule) objects             |
222: 
223: ### PatchTrafficFilterRequest
224: 
225: Used when updating a traffic filter (`PATCH`). All fields are optional; only included fields are updated.
226: 
227: | Field                | Type    | Required | Description                                                                  |
228: | -------------------- | ------- | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
229: | `name`               | string  | No       | Updated display name                                                         |
230: | `description`        | string  | No       | Updated description                                                          |
231: | `include_by_default` | boolean | No       | Updated auto-association flag                                                |
232: | `rules`              | array   | No       | Complete replacement list of [TrafficFilterRule](#trafficfilterrule) objects |
233: 
234: > `type` and `region` cannot be changed after creation.
235: 
236: ### TrafficFilterRule
237: 
238: A single rule within a traffic filter.
239: 
240: | Field         | Type   | Required | Description                                                                  |
241: | ------------- | ------ | -------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
242: | `source`      | string | No       | IP address, CIDR block (for `ip` type), or VPC endpoint ID (for `vpce` type) |
243: | `description` | string | No       | Human-readable description of this rule                                      |
244: 
245: ### TrafficFilterInfo
246: 
247: Returned by all read and write operations. Extends [TrafficFilterRequest](#trafficfilterrequest) with an `id` field.
248: 
249: | Field                | Type    | Description                                             |
250: | -------------------- | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------- |
251: | `id`                 | string  | Unique traffic filter ID (generated by the API)         |
252: | `name`               | string  | Display name                                            |
253: | `description`        | string  | Human-readable description                              |
254: | `type`               | string  | `ip` or `vpce`                                          |

261: ## Project Association
262: 
263: > **Official API docs:**
264: > [Patch Elasticsearch project](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elastic-cloud-serverless/operation/operation-patchelasticsearchproject)
265: > ·

267: > ·
268: > [Patch Security project](https://www.elastic.co/docs/api/doc/elastic-cloud-serverless/operation/operation-patchsecurityproject)
269: 
270: Traffic filters are associated with Serverless projects using the **project PATCH endpoint**, not through the traffic
271: filter API. This is handled by the **cloud-manage-project** skill.
272: 
273: ### Associate a filter with a project
274: 
275: ```text
276: PATCH /api/v1/serverless/projects/{type}/{id}
277: ```
278: 
279: Include the `traffic_filters` field with the **complete list** of filter IDs to associate:
280: 
281: ```json
282: {
283:   "traffic_filters": [{ "id": "tf-12345" }, { "id": "tf-67890" }]
284: }
285: ```
286: 
287: Any filter ID not included in the list is disassociated from the project. To remove all filters, send an empty array.
288: 
289: ### List projects associated with a filter
290: 
291: ```text
292: GET /api/v1/serverless/projects/{type}?traffic_filter={filter-id}
293: ```
294: 
295: Returns projects that have the specified filter associated.
296: 
297: ### Include filters at project creation
298: 
299: ```text
300: POST /api/v1/serverless/projects/{type}
301: ```

306: {
307:   "name": "my-project",
308:   "region_id": "us-ea"}}
